text:
Connor Hellebuyck asked Winnipeg for a trade, sat out the preseason and the start of the year, and became a Devil on Oct. 23. Yahoo News Canada headlined his explanation as "death threats motivated trade request out of Canada." He then won his first five games in New Jersey, the first goalie in team history to do it, before the Devils sat him for his return to Winnipeg. He starts here at .916 and +1.9 saved above expected in six games, and he is the fix a team that already controls play was missing: our numbers say New Jersey's goaltending has allowed 5.4 more goals than expected this season.

The Devils are the best five-on-five team in this game by a distance, with 58% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and they're better than even their +15 goal difference suggests (+21.0 expected). They won the first half of this home-and-home 5-2 on Thursday, a game that was closer to a coin flip on chances. Jack Hughes has points in seven straight, and our numbers have him at 41% to score. Jesper Bratt has ten points in his last six games against Washington. Luke Evangelista is one goal from 50. Anthony Mantha is out with a neck injury, and Connor Brown has taken his spot.

Washington's story is Alex Ovechkin's last season, and it's been a quiet one lately. TSN notes he's goalless in 11 straight; our count is twelve games without a goal on 3.9 expected goals, and two points in ten on 4.8 expected. Our numbers file that under bad luck rather than decline. The Capitals have also spent the week in the league's discipline conversation: Tom Wilson avoided a suspension for his hit on Sandis Vilmanis, and Jakob Chychrun's hit that knocked out Nick Cousins was ruled legal. Logan Thompson is at +1.4 this season after +28.2 last year.

Washington won the first meeting 4-2 on Oct. 17, a game the chances gave them only 27% of the time. Alex Tuch leads the Capitals at 36% to score. Our playoff odds: Devils 95%, Capitals 55%.
headline: Hellebuyck's Devils go back at the Capitals
